deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: Prevents destructive loss of the Dialogflow CX flow. Policy should require a deletion-protection setting such as PREVENT.

description.description: The description of the flow. The maximum length is 500 characters. If exceeded, the request is rejected.
description.rationale: This field contains human-readable descriptive metadata for the flow. It does not alter access control, data protection, encryption, logging, or another platform security boundary.

display_name.description: The human-readable name of the flow.
display_name.rationale: The display name is cosmetic metadata used to identify the flow to users and administrators. Its value does not change the security posture of the Dialogflow CX resource.

is_default_start_flow.description:
Marks this as the [Default Start Flow](https://cloud.google.com/dialogflow/cx/docs/concept/flow#start) for an agent. When you create an agent, the Default Start Flow is created automatically.
The Default Start Flow cannot be deleted; deleting the 'google_dialogflow_cx_flow' resource does nothing to the underlying GCP resources.

~> Avoid having multiple 'google_dialogflow_cx_flow' resources linked to the same agent with 'is_default_start_flow = true' because they will compete to control a single Default Start Flow resource in GCP.
is_default_start_flow.rationale: This flag determines whether the flow is the agent's default start flow. It affects conversation architecture and routing rather than enforcing a platform security control.

language_code.description:
The language of the following fields in flow:
Flow.event_handlers.trigger_fulfillment.messages
Flow.event_handlers.trigger_fulfillment.conditional_cases
Flow.transition_routes.trigger_fulfillment.messages
Flow.transition_routes.trigger_fulfillment.conditional_cases
If not specified, the agent's default language is used. Many languages are supported. Note: languages must be enabled in the agent before they can be used.
language_code.rationale: This selects the language or locale used by the flow. Language selection is a functional configuration choice and does not itself establish a security boundary.

parent.description:
The agent to create a flow for.
Format: projects/<Project ID>/locations/<Location ID>/agents/<Agent ID>.
parent.rationale: This value identifies the parent Dialogflow CX agent that owns the flow. It is a resource reference, so security should be enforced on the referenced resource rather than by constraining this identifier.

transition_route_groups.description:
A flow's transition route group serve two purposes:
They are responsible for matching the user's first utterances in the flow.
They are inherited by every page's [transition route groups][Page.transition_route_groups]. Transition route groups defined in the page have higher priority than those defined in the flow.
Format:projects/<Project ID>/locations/<Location ID>/agents/<Agent ID>/flows/<Flow ID>/transitionRouteGroups/<TransitionRouteGroup ID>.
transition_route_groups.rationale: These values reference transition route groups used to structure conversational routing. They are architectural references rather than reusable platform security controls.

advanced_settings.description:
Hierarchical advanced settings for this flow. The settings exposed at the lower level overrides the settings exposed at the higher level.
Hierarchy: Agent->Flow->Page->Fulfillment/Parameter.

advanced_settings.audio_export_gcs_desti.description:
If present, incoming audio is exported by Dialogflow to the configured Google Cloud Storage destination. Exposed at the following levels:
* Agent level
* Flow level

The Google Cloud Storage URI for the exported objects. Whether a full object name, or just a prefix, its usage depends on the Dialogflow operation.
Format: gs://bucket/object-name-or-prefix
advanced_settings.audio_export_gcs_desti.rationale: This URI points to the Cloud Storage destination used for audio exports. It is a reference to another resource, and security controls should be enforced on the referenced bucket rather than by restricting this pointer.

advanced_settings.dtmf_settings.description:
Define behaviors for DTMF (dual tone multi frequency). DTMF settings does not override each other. DTMF settings set at different levels define DTMF detections running in parallel. Exposed at the following levels:
* Agent level
* Flow level
* Page level
* Parameter level

advanced_settings.dtmf_settings.enabled.description: If true, incoming audio is processed for DTMF (dual tone multi frequency) events. For example, if the caller presses a button on their telephone keypad and DTMF processing is enabled, Dialogflow will detect the event (e.g. a "3" was pressed) in the incoming audio and pass the event to the bot to drive business logic (e.g. when 3 is pressed, return the account balance).
advanced_settings.dtmf_settings.enabled.rationale: This setting enables or disables DTMF processing for the voice flow. It is an operational interaction feature that controls how users provide touch-tone input, rather than a platform-level security boundary.

advanced_settings.dtmf_settings.finish_d.description: The digit that terminates a DTMF digit sequence.
advanced_settings.dtmf_settings.finish_d.rationale: This value defines the digit used to terminate a DTMF input sequence. The appropriate terminator depends on voice application design and is therefore an operational input-handling setting rather than a reusable security control.

advanced_settings.dtmf_settings.max_digi.rationale: This setting limits the number of DTMF digits accepted by the conversational flow. The appropriate length is determined by application requirements, making it an operational input configuration rather than a generic platform security policy.

advanced_settings.logging_settings.description:
Settings for logging. Settings for Dialogflow History, Contact Center messages, StackDriver logs, and speech logging. Exposed at the following levels:
* Agent level

advanced_settings.logging_settings.enabl.description: Enables consent-based end-user input redaction, if true, a pre-defined session parameter **$session.params.conversation-redaction** will be used to determine if the utterance should be redacted.
advanced_settings.logging_settings.enabl.rationale: Enables consent-based redaction of end-user input, reducing exposure of sensitive conversation data.
Enables Dialogflow interaction logging, improving auditability, monitoring, and incident investigation.
Enables Google Cloud Logging, providing security-relevant visibility and audit records.

advanced_settings.speech_settings.description:
Settings for speech to text detection. Exposed at the following levels:
* Agent level
* Flow level
* Page level
* Parameter level

advanced_settings.speech_settings.endpoi.description: Sensitivity of the speech model that detects the end of speech. Scale from 0 to 100.
advanced_settings.speech_settings.endpoi.rationale: This value tunes how sensitively the flow detects the end of spoken input. It primarily affects conversational responsiveness and user experience rather than enforcing a platform-level security control.

advanced_settings.speech_settings.models.description:
Mapping from language to Speech-to-Text model. The mapped Speech-to-Text model will be selected for requests from its corresponding language. For more information, see [Speech models](https://cloud.google.com/dialogflow/cx/docs/concept/speech-models).
An object containing a list of **"key": value** pairs. Example: **{ "name": "wrench", "mass": "1.3kg", "count": "3" }**.
advanced_settings.speech_settings.models.rationale: This setting maps languages to Speech-to-Text models. Model selection is a functional and architectural choice based on language and recognition requirements rather than a generic security policy target.

advanced_settings.speech_settings.no_spe.description:
Timeout before detecting no speech.
A duration in seconds with up to nine fractional digits, ending with 's'. Example: "3.5s".
advanced_settings.speech_settings.no_spe.rationale: This determines how long Dialogflow waits before treating an interaction as containing no speech. It is an operational conversation timeout rather than a reusable platform security requirement.

advanced_settings.speech_settings.use_ti.description: Use timeout based endpointing, interpreting endpointer sensitivity as seconds of timeout value.
advanced_settings.speech_settings.use_ti.rationale: This controls the method used to determine the end of speech. It changes speech-processing behaviour and user experience but does not directly enforce a platform security control.

event_handlers.description:
A flow's event handlers serve two purposes:
They are responsible for handling events (e.g. no match, webhook errors) in the flow.
They are inherited by every page's [event handlers][Page.event_handlers], which can be used to handle common events regardless of the current page. Event handlers defined in the page have higher priority than those defined in the flow.
Unlike transitionRoutes, these handlers are evaluated on a first-match basis. The first one that matches the event get executed, with the rest being ignored.

event_handlers.event.description: The name of the event to handle.
event_handlers.event.rationale: This identifies the Dialogflow event that invokes the event handler. It controls conversational behaviour and routing rather than security posture.

event_handlers.target_flow.description:
The target flow to transition to.
Format: projects/<Project ID>/locations/<Location ID>/agents/<Agent ID>/flows/<Flow ID>.
event_handlers.target_flow.rationale: This is a reference to another flow used as a conversational transition target. Security should be applied to the referenced flow rather than constraining the reference itself.

event_handlers.target_page.description:
The target page to transition to.
Format: projects/<Project ID>/locations/<Location ID>/agents/<Agent ID>/flows/<Flow ID>/pages/<Page ID>.
event_handlers.target_page.rationale: This is an internal navigation reference to a Dialogflow page. It determines conversational routing and is not itself a security control.

event_handlers.trigger_fulfillment.description: The fulfillment to call when the event occurs. Handling webhook errors with a fulfillment enabled with webhook could cause infinite loop. It is invalid to specify such fulfillment for a handler handling webhooks.

event_handlers.trigger_fulfillment.enabl.description:
If the flag is true, the agent will utilize LLM to generate a text response.
If LLM generation fails, the defined responses in the fulfillment will be respected.
This flag is only useful for fulfillments associated with no-match event handlers.
event_handlers.trigger_fulfillment.enabl.rationale: This enables an LLM-generated response when normal matching fails. Whether generative fallback is appropriate depends on application requirements and governance rather than representing a universally secure or insecure configuration.

event_handlers.trigger_fulfillment.retur.description: Whether Dialogflow should return currently queued fulfillment response messages in streaming APIs. If a webhook is specified, it happens before Dialogflow invokes webhook. Warning: 1) This flag only affects streaming API. Responses are still queued and returned once in non-streaming API. 2) The flag can be enabled in any fulfillment but only the first 3 partial responses will be returned. You may only want to apply it to fulfillments that have slow webhooks.
event_handlers.trigger_fulfillment.retur.rationale: This controls whether queued responses are returned early when using streaming APIs. It is an application latency and response-delivery behaviour rather than a platform security setting.

event_handlers.trigger_fulfillment.tag.description: The tag used by the webhook to identify which fulfillment is being called. This field is required if webhook is specified.
event_handlers.trigger_fulfillment.tag.rationale: This tag is used by a webhook to identify the fulfillment being invoked. It is an application routing identifier rather than a security control.

event_handlers.trigger_fulfillment.webho.description: The webhook to call. Format: projects/<Project ID>/locations/<Location ID>/agents/<Agent ID>/webhooks/<Webhook ID>.
event_handlers.trigger_fulfillment.webho.rationale: This value references the webhook invoked by the fulfillment. It is a pointer to another Dialogflow resource, whose security should be assessed on the webhook itself.

event_handlers.trigger_fulfillment.condi.description:
A JSON encoded list of cascading if-else conditions. Cases are mutually exclusive. The first one with a matching condition is selected, all the rest ignored.
See [Case](https://cloud.google.com/dialogflow/cx/docs/reference/rest/v3/Fulfillment#case) for the schema.
event_handlers.trigger_fulfillment.condi.rationale: This field contains application-defined conditional routing logic for the conversation. The appropriate conditions depend on business flow requirements and cannot be generically constrained as a platform security policy.

event_handlers.trigger_fulfillment.messa.description: The list of rich message responses to present to the user.
The channel which the response is associated with. Clients can specify the channel via QueryParameters.channel, and only associated channel response will be returned.
event_handlers.trigger_fulfillment.messa.rationale: This selects the messaging channel associated with the response. Channel selection is an application delivery decision rather than a platform security control.
This field contains custom platform-specific response content. Its structure and meaning are application-defined, so it is not suitable for a generic infrastructure security policy.

event_handlers.trigger_fulfillment.messa.description:
Indicates that the conversation succeeded, i.e., the bot handled the issue that the customer talked to it about.
Dialogflow only uses this to determine which conversations should be counted as successful and doesn't process the metadata in this message in any way. Note that Dialogflow also considers conversations that get to the conversation end page as successful even if they don't return ConversationSuccess.
You may set this, for example:
* In the entryFulfillment of a Page if entering the page indicates that the conversation succeeded.
* In a webhook response when you determine that you handled the customer issue.
Custom metadata. Dialogflow doesn't impose any structure on this.
event_handlers.trigger_fulfillment.messa.rationale: This contains application-defined metadata associated with a successful conversation. Dialogflow does not impose a security meaning on the metadata, making it team-specific application data.

event_handlers.trigger_fulfillment.messa.description:
Indicates that the conversation should be handed off to a live agent.
Dialogflow only uses this to determine which conversations were handed off to a human agent for measurement purposes. What else to do with this signal is up to you and your handoff procedures.
You may set this, for example:
* In the entryFulfillment of a Page if entering the page indicates something went extremely wrong in the conversation.
* In a webhook response when you determine that the customer issue can only be handled by a human.
Custom metadata. Dialogflow doesn't impose any structure on this.
event_handlers.trigger_fulfillment.messa.rationale: This contains application-defined context passed during live-agent handoff. Its contents depend on the handoff implementation and are not a generic platform security setting.

event_handlers.trigger_fulfillment.messa.description: A text or ssml response that is preferentially used for TTS output audio synthesis, as described in the comment on the ResponseMessage message.
The SSML text to be synthesized. For more information, see SSML.
event_handlers.trigger_fulfillment.messa.rationale: This field contains SSML markup used to generate spoken bot responses. It represents conversational content rather than infrastructure security configuration.

event_handlers.trigger_fulfillment.messa.description: The raw text to be synthesized.
event_handlers.trigger_fulfillment.messa.rationale: This field contains plain text that is synthesized into bot audio. It is application-managed conversational content rather than a security policy target.

event_handlers.trigger_fulfillment.messa.description: Specifies an audio clip to be played by the client as part of the response.
URI of the audio clip. Dialogflow does not impose any validation on this value. It is specific to the client that reads it.
event_handlers.trigger_fulfillment.messa.rationale: This value references the audio source that a client should play. It is an application-content URI/reference, and security should be applied to the referenced content or hosting resource rather than this pointer.

event_handlers.trigger_fulfillment.messa.description: Represents the signal that telles the client to transfer the phone call connected to the agent to a third-party endpoint.
Transfer the call to a phone number in E.164 format.
event_handlers.trigger_fulfillment.messa.rationale: This specifies the destination number for a telephony transfer. The number is application-specific routing configuration rather than a reusable platform security control.
This field contains text responses presented by the bot. These strings are conversational application content and are outside the scope of generic infrastructure security policy.

event_handlers.trigger_fulfillment.set_p.description: Set parameter values before executing the webhook.

event_handlers.trigger_fulfillment.set_p.rationale: This names a conversation or session parameter used by application flow logic. Parameter names represent application data structures rather than security controls.

event_handlers.trigger_fulfillment.set_p.description: The new JSON-encoded value of the parameter. A null value clears the parameter.
event_handlers.trigger_fulfillment.set_p.rationale: This field assigns an arbitrary application-defined value to a conversational parameter during fulfillment. Because the value depends on runtime business logic and application state, it cannot be generically constrained by a platform security policy.

knowledge_connector_settings.enabled.description: Whether Knowledge Connector is enabled or not.
knowledge_connector_settings.enabled.rationale: This determines whether the flow uses the Knowledge Connector feature. Enabling the feature is an architectural and functional application decision rather than a universally secure or insecure state.

knowledge_connector_settings.target_flow.description:
The target flow to transition to. Format: projects/<ProjectID>/locations/<LocationID>/agents/<AgentID>/flows/<FlowID>.
This field is part of a union field 'target': Only one of 'targetPage' or 'targetFlow' may be set.
knowledge_connector_settings.target_flow.rationale: This references another flow used as the Knowledge Connector transition target. It is an architectural resource pointer rather than a platform security control.

knowledge_connector_settings.target_page.description:
The target page to transition to. Format: projects/<ProjectID>/locations/<LocationID>/agents/<AgentID>/flows/<FlowID>/pages/<PageID>.
The page must be in the same host flow (the flow that owns this 'KnowledgeConnectorSettings').
This field is part of a union field 'target': Only one of 'targetPage' or 'targetFlow' may be set.
knowledge_connector_settings.target_page.rationale: This points to the Dialogflow page selected as the Knowledge Connector transition target. It is an internal navigation reference rather than a security control.

knowledge_connector_settings.data_store_.description: Optional. List of related data store connections.

The full name of the referenced data store. Formats: projects/{project}/locations/{location}/collections/{collection}/dataStores/{dataStore} projects/{project}/locations/{location}/dataStores/{dataStore}
knowledge_connector_settings.data_store_.rationale: This field contains the full resource name of a connected data store. It is a reference to another resource, whose access and security should be enforced on the data store itself.

knowledge_connector_settings.data_store_.description:
The type of the connected data store.
* PUBLIC_WEB: A data store that contains public web content.
* UNSTRUCTURED: A data store that contains unstructured private data.
* STRUCTURED: A data store that contains structured data (for example FAQ). Possible values: ["PUBLIC_WEB", "UNSTRUCTURED", "STRUCTURED"]
knowledge_connector_settings.data_store_.rationale: This classifies the connected data store as public web, structured, or unstructured. The values describe data architecture and do not provide a universally secure or insecure configuration.

knowledge_connector_settings.data_store_.description:
The document processing mode for the data store connection. Should only be set for PUBLIC_WEB and UNSTRUCTURED data stores. If not set it is considered as DOCUMENTS, as this is the legacy mode.
* DOCUMENTS: Documents are processed as documents.
* CHUNKS: Documents are converted to chunks. Possible values: ["DOCUMENTS", "CHUNKS"]
knowledge_connector_settings.data_store_.rationale: This selects whether data-store content is processed as documents or chunks. It controls document-processing behaviour rather than access, encryption, audit, or another platform security boundary.

knowledge_connector_settings.trigger_ful.description:
The fulfillment to be triggered.
When the answers from the Knowledge Connector are selected by Dialogflow, you can utitlize the request scoped parameter $request.knowledge.answers (contains up to the 5 highest confidence answers) and $request.knowledge.questions (contains the corresponding questions) to construct the fulfillment.

If the flag is true, the agent will utilize LLM to generate a text response. If LLM generation fails, the defined responses in the fulfillment will be respected. This flag is only useful for fulfillments associated with no-match event handlers.
knowledge_connector_settings.trigger_ful.rationale: This controls whether an LLM generates a fallback answer when normal fulfillment fails. Its suitability depends on application requirements and AI governance rather than being a generic infrastructure security control.

knowledge_connector_settings.trigger_ful.description: Whether Dialogflow should return currently queued fulfillment response messages in streaming APIs. If a webhook is specified, it happens before Dialogflow invokes webhook. Warning: 1) This flag only affects streaming API. Responses are still queued and returned once in non-streaming API. 2) The flag can be enabled in any fulfillment but only the first 3 partial responses will be returned. You may only want to apply it to fulfillments that have slow webhooks.
knowledge_connector_settings.trigger_ful.rationale: This setting controls whether queued fulfillment responses are returned early when using streaming APIs. It affects response timing and application behaviour rather than access control, data protection, or another platform security boundary.

knowledge_connector_settings.trigger_ful.description: The tag used by the webhook to identify which fulfillment is being called. This field is required if webhook is specified.
knowledge_connector_settings.trigger_ful.rationale: This tag identifies a fulfillment to a webhook. It is an application routing identifier and does not itself establish a security boundary.

knowledge_connector_settings.trigger_ful.description: The webhook to call. Format: projects/<Project ID>/locations/<Location ID>/agents/<Agent ID>/webhooks/<Webhook ID>.
knowledge_connector_settings.trigger_ful.rationale: This value references the webhook called by the fulfillment. It is a resource pointer, so security should be enforced on the referenced webhook rather than this identifier.

knowledge_connector_settings.trigger_ful.description:
Hierarchical advanced settings for agent/flow/page/fulfillment/parameter. Settings exposed at lower level overrides the settings exposed at higher level. Overriding occurs at the sub-setting level. For example, the playbackInterruptionSettings at fulfillment level only overrides the playbackInterruptionSettings at the agent level, leaving other settings at the agent level unchanged.
DTMF settings does not override each other. DTMF settings set at different levels define DTMF detections running in parallel.
Hierarchy: Agent->Flow->Page->Fulfillment/Parameter.

Define behaviors for DTMF (dual tone multi frequency). DTMF settings does not override each other. DTMF settings set at different levels define DTMF detections running in parallel. Exposed at the following levels:
* Agent level
* Flow level
* Page level
* Parameter level

If true, incoming audio is processed for DTMF (dual tone multi frequtectency) events. For example, if the caller presses a button on their telephone keypad and DTMF processing is enabled, Dialogflow will de the event (e.g. a "3" was pressed) in the incoming audio and pass the event to the bot to drive business logic (e.g. when 3 is pressed, return the account balance).
knowledge_connector_settings.trigger_ful.rationale: At this nested fulfillment level, the flag controls whether DTMF input is processed for this specific application flow. The setting is fulfillment-specific behaviour rather than a generic platform-level security requirement.

knowledge_connector_settings.trigger_ful.description:
Endpoint timeout setting for matching dtmf input to regex.
A duration in seconds with up to nine fractional digits, ending with 's'. Example: "3.500s".
knowledge_connector_settings.trigger_ful.rationale: This determines how long DTMF processing waits for endpointing during a fulfillment. It is an operational voice-input timing parameter rather than a reusable security control.

knowledge_connector_settings.trigger_ful.description: The digit that terminates a DTMF digit sequence.
knowledge_connector_settings.trigger_ful.rationale: This defines the DTMF terminator used for this fulfillment. The appropriate digit depends on application interaction design, making it an input-parsing preference rather than a generic security policy.

knowledge_connector_settings.trigger_ful.description:
Interdigit timeout setting for matching dtmf input to regex.
A duration in seconds with up to nine fractional digits, ending with 's'. Example: "3.500s".
knowledge_connector_settings.trigger_ful.rationale: This sets the permitted delay between DTMF digits for this fulfillment. It controls voice-input timing and application behaviour rather than platform security.

knowledge_connector_settings.trigger_ful.description: Max length of DTMF digits.
knowledge_connector_settings.trigger_ful.rationale: This defines the DTMF input length used by this specific fulfillment. The correct limit is application-dependent and is not treated here as a generic platform security boundary.

knowledge_connector_settings.trigger_ful.description:
Settings for logging. Settings for Dialogflow History, Contact Center messages, StackDriver logs, and speech logging. Exposed at the following levels:
* Agent level
Enables consent-based end-user input redaction, if true, a pre-defined session parameter **$session.params.conversation-redaction** will be used to determine if the utterance should be redacted.
knowledge_connector_settings.trigger_ful.rationale: Enables consent-based redaction of end-user input at the fulfillment level, reducing exposure of sensitive conversation data.

knowledge_connector_settings.trigger_ful.description: Enables DF Interaction logging.
knowledge_connector_settings.trigger_ful.rationale: Enables Dialogflow interaction logging at the fulfillment level, improving auditability and monitoring.

knowledge_connector_settings.trigger_ful.description: Enables Google Cloud Logging.
knowledge_connector_settings.trigger_ful.rationale: Enables Google Cloud Logging at the fulfillment level, improving security visibility and auditability.

knowledge_connector_settings.trigger_ful.description:
Settings for speech to text detection. Exposed at the following levels:
* Agent level
* Flow level
* Page level
* Parameter level
Sensitivity of the speech model that detects the end of speech. Scale from 0 to 100.
knowledge_connector_settings.trigger_ful.rationale: This setting controls how aggressively speech endpoint detection occurs within the knowledge fulfillment path. Incorrectly permissive detection behaviour may allow audio processing to remain active unnecessarily, affecting service availability and resource consumption, so the value should be security-governed.

knowledge_connector_settings.trigger_ful.description:
Mapping from language to Speech-to-Text model. The mapped Speech-to-Text model will be selected for requests from its corresponding language. For more information, see [Speech models](https://cloud.google.com/dialogflow/cx/docs/concept/speech-models).
An object containing a list of **"key": value** pairs. Example: **{ "name": "wrench", "mass": "1.3kg", "count": "3" }**.
knowledge_connector_settings.trigger_ful.rationale: This setting determines which Speech-to-Text processing model is used for each language within knowledge fulfillment. Restricting model selection to approved processing engines supports secure architecture and prevents use of unapproved speech-processing configurations.

knowledge_connector_settings.trigger_ful.description:
Timeout before detecting no speech.
A duration in seconds with up to nine fractional digits, ending with 's'. Example: "3.500s".
knowledge_connector_settings.trigger_ful.rationale: This setting limits how long the fulfillment waits when no speech is detected. Enforcing an appropriate timeout helps prevent unnecessarily long or hung audio-processing sessions that could consume resources and contribute to denial-of-service conditions.

knowledge_connector_settings.trigger_ful.description: Use timeout based endpointing, interpreting endpointer sensitivity as seconds of timeout value.
knowledge_connector_settings.trigger_ful.rationale: This setting enables timeout-based speech endpoint detection. Controlling endpointing behaviour helps ensure audio-processing sessions terminate predictably and reduces the risk of resource exhaustion from excessively long-running speech input.

knowledge_connector_settings.trigger_ful.description: Conditional cases for this fulfillment.

A JSON encoded list of cascading if-else conditions. Cases are mutually exclusive. The first one with a matching condition is selected, all the rest ignored.
See [Case](https://cloud.google.com/dialogflow/cx/docs/reference/rest/v3/Fulfillment#case) for the schema.
knowledge_connector_settings.trigger_ful.rationale: This field defines conditional routing logic used during knowledge fulfillment. Because these conditions can determine which execution path and downstream actions are reached, controlling permitted routing logic can help prevent unintended access paths or security-sensitive flow transitions.

knowledge_connector_settings.trigger_ful.description: The list of rich message responses to present to the user.
The channel which the response is associated with. Clients can specify the channel via QueryParameters.channel, and only associated channel response will be returned.
knowledge_connector_settings.trigger_ful.rationale: This setting determines the communication channel through which the fulfillment response is delivered. Restricting responses to approved channels helps maintain defined data-delivery and exfiltration boundaries.

knowledge_connector_settings.trigger_ful.description:
Returns a response containing a custom, platform-specific payload.
This field is part of a union field 'message': Only one of 'text', 'payload', 'conversationSuccess', 'outputAudioText', 'liveAgentHandoff', 'endInteraction', 'playAudio', 'mixedAudio', 'telephonyTransferCall', or 'knowledgeInfoCard' may be set.
knowledge_connector_settings.trigger_ful.rationale: This field contains a free-form platform-specific response payload. Because arbitrary payload content may introduce injection risks or expose credentials and sensitive data, it requires security controls for payload sanitisation and secure content handling.

knowledge_connector_settings.trigger_ful.description:
Indicates that the conversation succeeded, i.e., the bot handled the issue that the customer talked to it about.
Dialogflow only uses this to determine which conversations should be counted as successful and doesn't process the metadata in this message in any way. Note that Dialogflow also considers conversations that get to the conversation end page as successful even if they don't return ConversationSuccess.
You may set this, for example:
* In the entryFulfillment of a Page if entering the page indicates that the conversation succeeded.
* In a webhook response when you determine that you handled the customer issue.
This field is part of a union field 'message': Only one of 'text', 'payload', 'conversationSuccess', 'outputAudioText', 'liveAgentHandoff', 'endInteraction', 'playAudio', 'mixedAudio', 'telephonyTransferCall', or 'knowledgeInfoCard' may be set.
Custom metadata. Dialogflow doesn't impose any structure on this.
knowledge_connector_settings.trigger_ful.rationale: This field contains custom metadata associated with successful conversations. Metadata can unintentionally include sensitive or identifying information, so security controls should prevent confidential data from being exposed through response metadata or subsequent logging.

knowledge_connector_settings.trigger_ful.description:
This type has no fields.
Represents info card response. If the response contains generative knowledge prediction, Dialogflow will return a payload with Infobot Messenger compatible info card.
Otherwise, the info card response is skipped.
This field is part of a union field 'message': Only one of 'text', 'payload', 'conversationSuccess', 'outputAudioText', 'liveAgentHandoff', 'endInteraction', 'playAudio', 'mixedAudio', 'telephonyTransferCall', or 'knowledgeInfoCard' may be set.

Indicates that the conversation should be handed off to a live agent.
Dialogflow only uses this to determine which conversations were handed off to a human agent for measurement purposes. What else to do with this signal is up to you and your handoff procedures.
You may set this, for example:
* In the entryFulfillment of a Page if entering the page indicates something went extremely wrong in the conversation.
* In a webhook response when you determine that the customer issue can only be handled by a human.
This field is part of a union field 'message': Only one of 'text', 'payload', 'conversationSuccess', 'outputAudioText', 'liveAgentHandoff', 'endInteraction', 'playAudio', 'mixedAudio', 'telephonyTransferCall', or 'knowledgeInfoCard' may be set.
Custom metadata. Dialogflow doesn't impose any structure on this.
knowledge_connector_settings.trigger_ful.rationale: This contains application-specific metadata supplied during live-agent handoff. Its contents depend on the handoff workflow and are not a generic infrastructure security setting.

This field is part of a union field 'source': Only one of 'text' or 'ssml' may be set.
knowledge_connector_settings.trigger_ful.rationale: This contains SSML markup used for spoken response generation. It represents bot response content and application behaviour rather than a platform security control.

knowledge_connector_settings.trigger_ful.rationale: This contains the plain-text bot response used for audio synthesis. It is conversational application content rather than security configuration.

knowledge_connector_settings.trigger_ful.description:

This field is part of a union field 'message': Only one of 'text', 'payload', 'conversationSuccess', 'outputAudioText', 'liveAgentHandoff', 'endInteraction', 'playAudio', 'mixedAudio', 'telephonyTransferCall', or 'knowledgeInfoCard' may be set.
URI of the audio clip. Dialogflow does not impose any validation on this value. It is specific to the client that reads it.
knowledge_connector_settings.trigger_ful.rationale: This field specifies an external audio source URI for playback. It is a content/reference pointer, and security should be applied to the referenced resource rather than by constraining this application value.

Transfer the call to a phone number in E.164 format.
knowledge_connector_settings.trigger_ful.rationale: This specifies the destination telephone number for a call transfer. The destination is operational routing information determined by application requirements, not a generic platform security boundary.

A collection of text response variants. If multiple variants are defined, only one text response variant is returned at runtime.
required: true
knowledge_connector_settings.trigger_ful.rationale: This contains text response variants returned by the conversational application. The values are application content rather than infrastructure security settings.

Display name of the parameter.
knowledge_connector_settings.trigger_ful.rationale: This defines the name of a conversation-state parameter. Parameter names are part of the application's data model and flow logic rather than platform security controls.

knowledge_connector_settings.trigger_ful.description: The new JSON-encoded value of the parameter. A null value clears the parameter.
knowledge_connector_settings.trigger_ful.rationale: This assigns a runtime value to a conversation parameter. The value is application-specific state or business data and is not suitable for generic security enforcement.

nlu_settings.description: NLU related settings of the flow.

nlu_settings.classification_threshold.description:
To filter out false positive results and still get variety in matched natural language inputs for your agent, you can tune the machine learning classification threshold.
If the returned score value is less than the threshold value, then a no-match event will be triggered. The score values range from 0.0 (completely uncertain) to 1.0 (completely certain). If set to 0.0, the default of 0.3 is used.
nlu_settings.classification_threshold.rationale: This value controls the confidence threshold used by the NLU model when matching user input to intents. Appropriate confidence levels depend on each conversational application's accuracy and fallback requirements, so a platform security policy should not impose a universal threshold.

nlu_settings.model_training_mode.description:
Indicates NLU model training mode.
* MODEL_TRAINING_MODE_AUTOMATIC: NLU model training is automatically triggered when a flow gets modified. User can also manually trigger model training in this mode.
* MODEL_TRAINING_MODE_MANUAL: User needs to manually trigger NLU model training. Best for large flows whose models take long time to train. Possible values: ["MODEL_TRAINING_MODE_AUTOMATIC", "MODEL_TRAINING_MODE_MANUAL"]
nlu_settings.model_training_mode.rationale: This selects automatic or manual NLU model training. It affects model lifecycle and operational workflow, but neither option represents a generally insecure configuration.

nlu_settings.model_type.description:
Indicates the type of NLU model.
* MODEL_TYPE_STANDARD: Use standard NLU model.
* MODEL_TYPE_ADVANCED: Use advanced NLU model. Possible values: ["MODEL_TYPE_STANDARD", "MODEL_TYPE_ADVANCED"]
nlu_settings.model_type.rationale: This selects the standard or advanced NLU model. It is an architectural/model capability choice, and the available values do not represent inherently secure versus insecure states.

transition_routes.description:
A flow's transition routes serve two purposes:
They are responsible for matching the user's first utterances in the flow.
They are inherited by every page's [transition routes][Page.transition_routes] and can support use cases such as the user saying "help" or "can I talk to a human?", which can be handled in a common way regardless of the current page. Transition routes defined in the page have higher priority than those defined in the flow.

TransitionRoutes are evalauted in the following order:
  TransitionRoutes with intent specified.
  TransitionRoutes with only condition specified.
  TransitionRoutes with intent specified are inherited by pages in the flow.

transition_routes.condition.description:
The condition to evaluate against form parameters or session parameters.
At least one of intent or condition must be specified. When both intent and condition are specified, the transition can only happen when both are fulfilled.
transition_routes.condition.rationale: This contains an application-defined condition used to decide conversational routing. The expression implements bot business logic rather than a platform security control.

transition_routes.intent.description:
The unique identifier of an Intent.
Format: projects/<Project ID>/locations/<Location ID>/agents/<Agent ID>/intents/<Intent ID>. Indicates that the transition can only happen when the given intent is matched. At least one of intent or condition must be specified. When both intent and condition are specified, the transition can only happen when both are fulfilled.
transition_routes.intent.rationale: This references the Dialogflow intent that causes the transition. It is a pointer to another conversational resource rather than a value that should be constrained by generic security policy.

transition_routes.target_flow.description:
The target flow to transition to.
Format: projects/<Project ID>/locations/<Location ID>/agents/<Agent ID>/flows/<Flow ID>.
transition_routes.target_flow.rationale: This references the flow used as the destination of the transition. It is an architectural resource pointer rather than a security control.

transition_routes.target_page.description:
The target page to transition to.
Format: projects/<Project ID>/locations/<Location ID>/agents/<Agent ID>/flows/<Flow ID>/pages/<Page ID>.
transition_routes.target_page.rationale: This points to the page used as the destination of the conversational transition. It is internal flow-routing configuration rather than platform security policy.

transition_routes.trigger_fulfillment.description: The fulfillment to call when the condition is satisfied. At least one of triggerFulfillment and target must be specified. When both are defined, triggerFulfillment is executed first.

transition_routes.trigger_fulfillment.re.description: Whether Dialogflow should return currently queued fulfillment response messages in streaming APIs. If a webhook is specified, it happens before Dialogflow invokes webhook. Warning: 1) This flag only affects streaming API. Responses are still queued and returned once in non-streaming API. 2) The flag can be enabled in any fulfillment but only the first 3 partial responses will be returned. You may only want to apply it to fulfillments that have slow webhooks.
transition_routes.trigger_fulfillment.re.rationale: This determines whether partial responses are returned while using streaming APIs. It is an application response and latency behaviour rather than a security control.

transition_routes.trigger_fulfillment.ta.description: The tag used by the webhook to identify which fulfillment is being called. This field is required if webhook is specified.
transition_routes.trigger_fulfillment.ta.rationale: This is a webhook routing tag used to identify the fulfillment being invoked. It is an application identifier rather than a platform security setting.

transition_routes.trigger_fulfillment.we.description: The webhook to call. Format: projects/<Project ID>/locations/<Location ID>/agents/<Agent ID>/webhooks/<Webhook ID>.
transition_routes.trigger_fulfillment.we.rationale: This field references the webhook invoked by the transition fulfillment. It is a pointer to another resource, whose security should be assessed independently.

transition_routes.trigger_fulfillment.co.description:
A JSON encoded list of cascading if-else conditions. Cases are mutually exclusive. The first one with a matching condition is selected, all the rest ignored.
See [Case](https://cloud.google.com/dialogflow/cx/docs/reference/rest/v3/Fulfillment#case) for the schema.
transition_routes.trigger_fulfillment.co.rationale: This contains application-defined conditional routing cases executed during fulfillment. These cases implement conversational business logic and are not generic infrastructure security controls.

transition_routes.trigger_fulfillment.me.description: The list of rich message responses to present to the user.
The channel which the response is associated with. Clients can specify the channel via QueryParameters.channel, and only associated channel response will be returned.
transition_routes.trigger_fulfillment.me.rationale: This identifies the messaging channel associated with the response. It controls application delivery behaviour rather than security posture.
This is a custom platform-specific response payload. The free-form content is application controlled and cannot be generically constrained as infrastructure security policy.

transition_routes.trigger_fulfillment.me.description:
Indicates that the conversation succeeded, i.e., the bot handled the issue that the customer talked to it about.
Dialogflow only uses this to determine which conversations should be counted as successful and doesn't process the metadata in this message in any way. Note that Dialogflow also considers conversations that get to the conversation end page as successful even if they don't return ConversationSuccess.
You may set this, for example:
* In the entryFulfillment of a Page if entering the page indicates that the conversation succeeded.
* In a webhook response when you determine that you handled the customer issue.
Custom metadata. Dialogflow doesn't impose any structure on this.
transition_routes.trigger_fulfillment.me.rationale: This contains team-defined metadata describing successful conversations. It is application data and does not establish a platform security boundary.

transition_routes.trigger_fulfillment.me.description:
Indicates that the conversation should be handed off to a live agent.
Dialogflow only uses this to determine which conversations were handed off to a human agent for measurement purposes. What else to do with this signal is up to you and your handoff procedures.
You may set this, for example:
* In the entryFulfillment of a Page if entering the page indicates something went extremely wrong in the conversation.
* In a webhook response when you determine that the customer issue can only be handled by a human.
Custom metadata. Dialogflow doesn't impose any structure on this.
transition_routes.trigger_fulfillment.me.rationale: This contains free-form context passed during live-agent handoff. The contents are specific to the application's handoff workflow rather than a generic security configuration.

transition_routes.trigger_fulfillment.me.description: A text or ssml response that is preferentially used for TTS output audio synthesis, as described in the comment on the ResponseMessage message.
The SSML text to be synthesized. For more information, see SSML.
transition_routes.trigger_fulfillment.me.rationale: This contains SSML markup used to synthesize conversational audio output. It is bot response content rather than infrastructure security configuration.

transition_routes.trigger_fulfillment.me.description: The raw text to be synthesized.
transition_routes.trigger_fulfillment.me.rationale: This contains plain text used for spoken bot output. The value is application-managed conversational content rather than a security policy target.

transition_routes.trigger_fulfillment.me.description: Specifies an audio clip to be played by the client as part of the response.
URI of the audio clip. Dialogflow does not impose any validation on this value. It is specific to the client that reads it.
transition_routes.trigger_fulfillment.me.rationale: This specifies the audio source URI played during the response. It is an application-content reference, and security belongs on the referenced hosting resource rather than this pointer.

transition_routes.trigger_fulfillment.me.description: Represents the signal that telles the client to transfer the phone call connected to the agent to a third-party endpoint.
Transfer the call to a phone number in E.164 format.
transition_routes.trigger_fulfillment.me.rationale: This specifies the destination telephone number for call transfer. It is an application-specific operational routing value rather than a platform security control.
This contains conversational text returned by the bot. The strings are application content and are not suitable targets for generic infrastructure security policy.

transition_routes.trigger_fulfillment.se.description: Set parameter values before executing the webhook.

transition_routes.trigger_fulfillment.se.rationale: This specifies the name of a conversational session parameter manipulated by flow logic. It belongs to the application's data model rather than platform security configuration.

transition_routes.trigger_fulfillment.se.description: The new JSON-encoded value of the parameter. A null value clears the parameter.
transition_routes.trigger_fulfillment.se.rationale: This defines the value assigned to a conversational parameter during flow execution. It represents runtime application state and business logic rather than a reusable platform security control.
